commit.author: Stelian Vultur
commit.message: implement issue #2297 : Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code

requirement.title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement.summary: MessagePack-generated code should be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage so it does not skew coverage results. The thread includes a coverage-tool workaround and a proposed template-based implementation, but no maintainer decision on those proposals.

criteria.text: All MessagePack-generated code is decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage.
criteria.summary: All MessagePack-generated code must use ExcludeFromCodeCoverage

criteria.text: Users can obtain the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage decoration without being required to configure a new setting; an optional setting is permissible but not required.
criteria.summary: ExcludeFromCodeCoverage must apply by default without requiring configuration

open_questions: Should the implementation follow armadavalor's proposal to add the fully qualified attribute to the formatter, string-key formatter, enum/union formatter, and resolver templates and update the verified snapshots, or should users instead be directed to coverage-tool configuration such as b-kurczynski-dl's dotnet-coverage exclusion?
Should generated types also receive GeneratedCode("MessagePack.SourceGenerator", <version>), as armadavalor suggested?
Should the attribute always be emitted, or should an optional setting control it?
requirement.short: MessagePack-generated code must have ExcludeFromCodeCoverage to avoid skewing coverage

environment: Linux only: net472 targets and Windows-only tests did not run

hunks.context: Two assembly-level attributes exist to help with mixing in your own custom forma
lines: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).
+All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so generated code does not skew code coverage reports.
+The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework).

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.

suspicions.hypothesis: Removing the attribute from either FormatterCache<T> or GetFormatterHelper in ResolverTemplate would still leave both new coverage tests passing: they require only one attribute somewhere in each generated file and validate only the occurrences that exist, rather than associating an attribute with every generated type.

The conditional guards may not compile correctly for all supported target frameworks, but the new tests would not reveal that because they inspect generated text using the default reference set and never compile the generated output with NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK defined.

The new coverage-test source does not exercise CompositeResolverTemplate, so a missing or malformed composite-resolver decoration would rely solely on the separate composite-resolver snapshot tests rather than the new requirement-focused tests.

H10's anyConstraints branch may be unexercised by the listed tests; a formatter nested inside a generic containing type with constraints is needed to demonstrate that the revised brace and newline emission produces the intended valid output.

probes.title: ResolverTemplate FormatterCache decoration is required for its own type
probes.hypothesis: The new coverage tests only require one ExcludeFromCodeCoverage occurrence per generated file and validate only existing occurrences, so removing the attribute from FormatterCache<T> in ResolverTemplate would leave both tests green; the requirement REQ-2297.1 demands all generated code decorated, so a per-type association check should fail if any generated type lacks the attribute.
criteria: For the resolver generated file, count generated type declarations (class/struct) and count ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attributes appearing immediately before a type declaration; assert every type declaration in the resolver file is immediately preceded by the attribute (possibly via guard).
probes.means: If the test fails, it shows the resolver file has generated types (e.g. GetFormatterHelper or FormatterCache<T>) not immediately decorated, refuting C4/C8's claim that all generated code is decorated, and demonstrating the coverage tests are too weak to catch it.

criteria: Generate a composite resolver; textually substitute the guards so the NETFRAMEWORK/netstandard2.0 branch is taken (i.e., strip #if lines treating them as false) does not work; instead compile generated output with preprocessor symbols NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK defined and the attribute type unavailable, expecting compile errors if guard is wrong. The new tests do not compile generated output, so they miss this.
probes.means: If it fails, the guard placement is wrong: the attribute leaks through preprocessing under netstandard2.0/.NET Framework, so generated code that defines those symbols would fail to compile, directly refuting the guarded layout claims and the new tests that only inspect text without preprocessing.

probes.title: H10 anyConstraints branch yields syntactically valid nested generic formatter
probes.hypothesis: Changing the brace/newline emission for the anyConstraints=true branch was needed to keep attribute placement valid, but the new tests never exercise a formatter nested in a generic containing type with constraints, so a regression in that branch (syntax or attribute placement) is undetected. A nested generic type with a constraint should produce a parseable type declaration whose opening brace placement is consistent (brace on its own line with newline after).
criteria: Generate a formatter for a type nested inside a generic outer type with a type parameter constraint; assert the generated file parses without syntax errors and that the nesting type constraint line is followed by an opening brace on its own line with no stray non-whitespace token before the brace.
probes.means: If it fails, the anyConstraints branch produces malformed brace/newline emission or attribute placement for nested constrained formatters, refuting C6/REQ-2297.1 for that case and showing the listed tests don't cover it.

rounds.reason: The output contains no assertion message, exception details, or generated text, so it does not identify which assertion failed or whether the failure concerns brace placement at all. The probe also fails at the base commit, so the summary alone does not establish a regression introduced by the change. It could instead be failing during formatter discovery, on its exact line-layout assumption, or on parse diagnostics; the supplied output does not distinguish these possibilities.

Both revisions report only the same test-level failure, without the failing assertion, generated text, or diagnostics. The probe can fail at several distinct points, including its brittle exact-line constraint/brace checks and the final whole-compilation assertion, and these failures would have different implications. Thus the output does not establish that the head failed because of the hypothesized anyConstraints regression rather than a probe or fixture problem; the identical base summary does not resolve that ambiguity.

The failing assertion is a whole-compilation error check, and it fails on CS0246 errors for an unresolved `T` in `GeneratedMessagePackResolver.g.cs`, not on brace placement, parsing, or attribute placement in the constrained nested formatter. The generated-formatter syntax-error assertion passed, and the base fails with the same resolver errors (only line numbers shift), so the failure is unrelated to the hypothesized regression and does not show that the changed code behaves wrongly.

The hypothesis that H10's anyConstraints branch produces invalid output is not demonstrable with a failing probe: the unchanged noConstraints path and the new anyConstraints path both emit a newline after the opening brace, and the nested generic formatter for `Container<T>.Nested` parses without syntax errors at the head. The only compilation errors observed (unresolved `T` in the generated resolver) stem from the resolver template's handling of the containing generic type and occur identically at the base, so they do not show the brace/newline change is wrong. No correct probe of this hypothesis is expected to fail, hence give up.

refusals.question: Does REQ-2297.1's requirement that all generated code be decorated permit omitting the attribute entirely when NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK is defined, rather than supplying or otherwise accommodating the attribute on those targets?
refusals.why: The implementation and documentation choose a target-dependent exception to the otherwise unconditional requirement. The issue records no maintainer decision on the proposed implementation, so this interpretation of the required behavior belongs to the owner.
